items.title: Jodie Foster Says Brad Pitt's 'F1' Seemed Like It Was Made by AI and Written by a Computer: 'Wasn't It?'
items.summary: At the Aspen Festival of Ideas talk 'Who Owns the Future of Hollywood,' Jodie Foster quipped that Apple's blockbuster 'F1' seemed like it could have been made by AI and written by a computer. She allowed that AI tools are useful for 'small helpful things' like previs, while questioning formula-driven studio filmmaking in the AI era.
items.why: A-list Oscar winner publicly drawing the line between AI-formula filmmaking and human authorship, aimed at one of 2026's biggest hits — high-conversation AI x film story.
items.notes: Deadline ran the same story (deadline.com/2026/07/jodie-foster-thinks-f1-was-made-with-ai-wasnt-it-1236973717/, 2026-07-02) — de-duped; Variety kept for outlet diversity.

items.title: 'The Sopranos' Creator David Chase, Jude Law's Riff Raff, Demystifying AI: KVIFF Industry Days Primer
items.summary: Karlovy Vary's expanded Industry Days (July 5-8) puts 'demystifying AI' on the main stage: a hands-on presentation of currently available AI tools for film professionals, plus sessions on microdramas and other disruption threats, per KVIFF Film Industry Office head Hugo Rosak. The 60th edition frames AI literacy as a core skill for European film pros.
items.why: Major European festival institutionalizing AI-tools education for the film industry — festival-circuit AI adoption angle beyond Hollywood.
items.notes: Angle for the card should be the AI/microdrama program, not the Sopranos/Jude Law business items.

items.title: 'Sheep in the Box' Trailer: Hirokazu Koreeda Makes a Plea for Imagination in the AI Age with Sci-Fi Grief Drama
items.summary: Neon released the trailer for Hirokazu Koreeda's Cannes-premiered sci-fi grief drama 'Sheep in the Box' (in US theaters July 24), in which a Japanese couple welcomes an AI-powered android re-creation of their deceased son into their home — Koreeda's plea for human imagination in the AI age.
items.why: Master filmmaker's on-screen reckoning with AI companionship and grief, arriving in theaters via Neon — the culture-side counterweight to tool news.
items.notes: Film itself is about AI (theme), not AI-made; distinct from published Neon/'Artificial' story though Neon distributes both.

items.title: AI Just Collects 'Our Old Ideas', Paul Feig Declares; 'We Are HI: Human Intelligence'
items.summary: Writer-director Paul Feig ('Bridesmaids') derided generative AI as 'an amalgamation of our old ideas,' arguing that the technology can only recombine what humans already made and coining 'HI — human intelligence' as the industry's real engine.
items.why: Working studio director articulating the creative case against generative AI — pairs as counterpoint to studio-adoption coverage.
items.notes: Deadline already heavy in published set; keep only if outlet mix allows (1 Deadline item in this batch).

items.title: Tony Leung Reflects on the Rise of AI and His Hopes for the Future of Film
items.summary: Heading the Golden Goblet jury in Shanghai, Tony Leung discussed AI's threat to creativity, how cinema can keep young audiences in theaters, and his late-career move into European arthouse work — an Asian-cinema icon's measured take on the AI era.
items.why: Asia angle on the AI x film debate from one of the most respected actors alive; diversifies geography beyond Hollywood.
items.notes: Distinct from already-published Variety 'Shanghai 2026 takeaways' piece (different outlet, different story: personal interview vs festival wrap). Near window edge (~318h old) — verify before publish day drift.
